advisories.summary: In FRRouting, bgpd accepts a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) whose outer TLV length does...
advisories.description: In FRRouting, bgpd accepts a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) whose outer TLV length does not match the length of the attribute: the mismatch is only logged and the attribute is processed anyway. A BGP neighbor can send UPDATE messages carrying such an attribute that put the reference count of the attribute's interned sub-TLV chain out of balance, so that the chain is freed while routes stored by bgpd (Adj-RIB-In entries and RIB paths) still point to it. When those routes are later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, bgpd reads the freed memory, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. The issue was reproduced with "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured for the neighbor, and the reporter observed that the crash does not occur on every attempt.

cwes.name: Double Free

advisories.summary: When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully...
advisories.description:
When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

advisories.summary: Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to...
advisories.description:
Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine.

read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session.

A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.
